skill.name: when-bridging-web-cli-use-web-cli-teleport
skill.description: Guide for building a local bridge between web interfaces and CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Build a local web-to-CLI bridge with REST and WebSocket examples.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The core workflow intentionally builds a browser-accessible bridge that executes CLI commands. Many Markdown fence detections are false positives, but the Node.js server example contains unauthenticated shell execution, wildcard CORS, WebSocket broadcasting, and command output exposure.

remediation.suggestion: Remove shell-string exec usage. Use spawn with fixed binaries, strict argument validation, authentication, authorization, and a command allowlist.

remediation.issue: Permissive CORS and unauthenticated WebSocket channels
remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed origins, require authenticated socket sessions, isolate channels per user, and redact command output before broadcast.

remediation.issue: Documentation treats localhost command execution as normal setup
remediation.suggestion: Add a threat model, explicit local-only warnings, sandboxing requirements, and production blockers before any bridge is exposed.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx and npm commands in setup scripts
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, document dependency review, and require confirmation before generated workflows install or run external tools.

content.user_title: Connect Web Interfaces to CLI Workflows
content.value_statement: Teams often need browser controls for local command workflows. This skill outlines a web-to-CLI bridge with REST, WebSocket, test, and deployment steps.
actual_capabilities: Outlines a phased architecture for a web-to-CLI bridge.
Shows commands to scaffold a React client and Express bridge server.
Includes REST and WebSocket examples for command output streaming.
Provides curl and npm test steps for integration checks.
Includes Docker and Prometheus setup notes for deployment.
limitations: The examples require strong security review before use.
The server example lacks authentication, authorization, and command allowlisting.
The workflow assumes Node.js, npm, Docker, and local port 3001.
It does not provide production-ready error handling or auditing.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Local Control Panel
use_cases.description: Create a browser interface that triggers approved local CLI workflows during development.

use_cases.title: Plan an Automation Bridge
use_cases.description: Map REST and WebSocket responsibilities before building an internal automation dashboard.

use_cases.title: Document Integration Boundaries
use_cases.description: Describe how browser UI, bridge APIs, and command-line tools exchange state and output.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the Bridge
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a local web-to-CLI bridge for my project. Include components, data flow, and setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design the API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define REST and WebSocket endpoints for a local CLI bridge. Include request flow and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review the Security Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a proposed web-to-CLI bridge. Identify authentication, authorization, CORS, and command execution risks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Production Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to adapt the bridge for production. Require command allowlists, audit logs, rate limits, and monitoring checks.

output_examples.input: Ask for a local bridge architecture.
output_examples.output: A phased plan with REST endpoints, a WebSocket channel, a React UI, and bridge server responsibilities.

output_examples.input: Ask to test command output streaming.
output: Latency and response targets to monitor.

output_examples.input: Ask for a production readiness review.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering authentication, command allowlisting, rate limiting, logging, and deployment monitoring.

best_practices: Treat all browser-provided commands and arguments as untrusted input.
Use explicit command allowlists and avoid shell string execution.
Bind local bridges to trusted origins and require authentication.
anti_patterns: Do not expose arbitrary command execution through a browser-accessible API.
Do not use wildcard CORS for endpoints that can start local processes.
Do not publish command output to every connected socket by default.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps plan and scaffold a local bridge between a web interface and CLI workflows.

faq.question: Does it provide production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. The examples need authentication, allowlisting, sandboxing, and audit logging before production use.

faq.question: Which tools does the workflow assume?
faq.answer: It assumes Node.js, npm, React, Express, Socket.io, curl, Docker, and local development tooling.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The example bridge accepts browser input and executes it as shell commands without adequate controls.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Use it as an architecture reference, then add strict authorization, command allowlists, and sandboxed execution.
